translation_notes: The mechanical draft wrote 'g2 += g{ {IRI[s_]} sem:{p_} {IRI[d_]} }' inside a plain 'for s_, p_, d_ in en.NEW_RELATIONS:' -- the biais mecanique the batch instructions warn about. Rewrote as the stratum's target idiom: '@graph g2' once before the loop, 'for @bindings in [...]:' reshaping each (s_, p_, d_) tuple into a row dict ({"s": IRI[s_], "p": p_, "d": IRI[d_]}), and a single '+{ ?s sem:{?p} ?d }' per row. Classified minor-restructuring for that reshaping (NEW_RELATIONS is a list of positional tuples, not already an iterable of mappings), not for anything RDF-semantic: same triples, same graph.

?s and ?d carry IRI[s_]/IRI[d_] -- URIRef objects already computed via cls_iri(n) = SEM[id + '_' + sanitised label], which concatenates the taxonomy id with a regex-cleaned label, not just the bare id -- so they cannot be rebuilt from a bare id via sem:{?id} local-part instantiation the way ?p can. Kept as pre-resolved terms passed through bindings (node() coercion passes an already-RDF term through unchanged, confirmed in terms.md's f{URIRef(...)} example and empirically for '?var' the same way). ?p uses sem:{?p} instead, since SEM[p_] in the original is exact string concatenation of the property name onto the sem: namespace -- the same idiom as ex:{name} in terms.md -- and p_ is always a plain camelCase identifier (stewardedBy, buildsOn, informs, ...) with no space or slash, so concatenation is safe and e<...> is not needed.

Context shim (context_predecl.py): BASEDIR, load(), nodes and cls_iri are all defined earlier in the same source file, outside this 2-line region. nodes is reduced to the 15 taxonomy entries en.NEW_RELATIONS references (verified against the real repository at altunelyusuf/SemanticTechnologies@bad0fa7c46: taxonomy_v1_0_0.py's TAX, real id/label pairs copied verbatim), not the full 59-entry taxonomy the real file builds -- the other 44 leaves are never read by this region. enrichment_n_v6_0_0.py (holding NEW_RELATIONS) is copied verbatim in full. semtech_tbox_v6_2_0.ttl is a minimal placeholder: this region only ADDS to g2, it never reads the pre-existing ~1000-triple ontology, so the placeholder's actual content cannot affect correctness (see that file's own header).

Sabotage-tested: retargeting the object of +{ } from ?d to ?s (so every relation triple wrongly points back at its own subject) makes rdfeval check fail (graphs not isomorphic, 9 vs 9 triples -- same count, different edges); restored before finalising.

Repair 2026-10-30: the prefix is now `semtech:`, not `sem:` (supersedes 'SEM->sem' above). The real semtech_tbox_v6_2_0.ttl binds `semtech:` to http://example.org/semtech#, and `@graph g2` under `@prefix sem:` rebound that namespace to `sem:`, dropping `semtech:` from g2 -- which the repository serialises later (build_core_v6_3_0.py:207), so the tbox it writes changed its prefixes. Hidden because the placeholder tbox itself declared `sem:`; with the real header copied into it, the driver's binding check failed on the old translation (('semtech', 'http://example.org/semtech#') missing) and passes with `@prefix semtech:`.

repair.driver: renforcé : le tbox de substitution porte les huit lignes @prefix du vrai semtech_tbox_v6_2_0.ttl (semtech:, et non plus sem:), et le pilote, après le verdict module-state de run_pair inchangé, exige que chaque liaison de préfixe du g2 de l'original se retrouve dans celui de la traduction (le dépôt sérialise g2 à la ligne 207)
mutants_killed: objet pris dans la colonne du sujet
@prefix sem: au lieu de semtech: (liaison semtech: écrasée par @graph) -- tué par la seule vérification des liaisons

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the two-line loop becomes one `g2 += ((IRI[s_], SEM[p_], IRI[d_]) for s_, p_, d_ in en.NEW_RELATIONS)`; Graph.__iadd__ is typed Iterable[triple] in rdflib 7.2.1, so this is the documented bulk add, not a trick. It saves 2 tokens and a line, and s_/p_/d_ no longer leak to module level (the driver compares only the names both sides define).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph g2` + `for s_, p_, d_ in en.NEW_RELATIONS:` + `+{ {IRI[s_]} semtech:{p_} {IRI[d_]} }`. The `for @bindings in [dict comprehension]` of translated.ldpy only reshaped the tuples into rows, so direct interpolation is shorter. A bulk `g2 += ((IRI[s_], semtech:{p_}, IRI[d_]) for ...)` measures the same 96 tokens and hardly uses the notation, so the island form was kept.

No exception to the symmetry rule. The notation gains nothing here: `semtech:{p_}` replaces `SEM[p_]` token for token, and the `@prefix` line of the fixed header makes optimized.ldpy 2 tokens longer than optimized.py.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: nothing unused in the header (Graph, Namespace, the four shim names and the SEM namespace are all used); a byte copy of optimized.py.

optimized_header.ldpy: the line `SEM = Namespace(...)` and the `Namespace` import go, because the `semtech:` prefix replaces them. The `@prefix semtech:` line stays: it is used, and `@graph g2` must bind it (the driver checks g2's prefix bindings).
